name: Tōkaidō Shinkansen high-speed rail
description: A dedicated high-speed railway provided intercity passenger travel in Japan.

places.note: Modern country or regional reference; historic political boundaries are not implied.

date.label: 1 October 1964
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: The Tōkaidō Shinkansen opened passenger service in Japan, linking Tokyo and Osaka.
events.caveats: Later service speed and trip times evolved; opening figures are not projected onto all later years.

evidence.supports: The National Railway Museum gives the opening day and major cities.

date.label: 2 May 1961
date.basis: Dated World Bank press release announcing the loan.

events.statement: The World Bank announced an $80 million equivalent loan to Japanese National Railways for the new Tokaido line.
events.caveats: The loan amount is a nominal commitment, not the final construction cost or evidence of all funds disbursed.

evidence.supports: Contemporary lender announces an $80 million loan to Japanese National Railways.

contributions.resource: Loan to Japanese National Railways for the new line

earliest_record.rationale: The 1964 opening is the earliest event establishing passenger-service availability for this capability; the 1961 loan is an earlier funding commitment, not operation.

caveats: High-speed experiments and train services predated this line; no global priority claimed.

measures.subject: Tokyo–Osaka at opening
measures.conditions: JR Central retrospective gives four hours at inauguration; later fastest times differ.

evidence.supports: The operator reports four hours at launch.

measures.subject: World Bank loan to Japanese National Railways
measures.money_context: Nominal 1961 US-dollar equivalent; not total final construction cost.
measures.conditions: Lender press release dated 2 May 1961; loan commitment, not proof of disbursement.

evidence.supports: Press release announces loan equivalent to $80 million.
